OmniDiff just entered the open‑source arena, promising a Rust‑based Git diff that’s both blister‑fast and content‑aware, according to its GitHub README.

The tool claims to correctly diff 99.95 % of code changes and complete typical diff operations in under 100 ms on an Intel i7‑1370P laptop.

It ships pre‑built binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows and is also available via Homebrew, Debian/Ubuntu APT packages, and Nix flakes, removing the need to compile from source.

“Fast, robust, accurate content‑aware diffing” is the project's own description of its goal.

This matters because developers can now see semantic changes in PDFs, images, fonts and other binary assets, reducing noise in code reviews and speeding up CI pipelines.

The performance numbers come from benchmarks on a Lenovo T14s with 32 GB RAM, and the accuracy figures reflect the project's test suite, which notes limited PDF test cases.

Would you consider swapping your current diff tool for a content‑aware alternative?

Full breakdown with sources: https://buildwithsaksham.in/blog/omnidiff-a-super-fast-content-aware-git-diff-tool-built-in-r
